# how to use a rule

```
guidance: cps.cma
for: cma1990.s1
written by: Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-10-29, standing in for the small model (Luna or Haiku)
source: CPS legal guidance, Computer Misuse Act, as in source/cps_cma_guidance.txt
licence of the source: Open Government Licence v3.0, Crown copyright
```

person: a thing that can know, can say what it can do, and can do it
element: a part of a rule that has to be true
evidence: data that says an element is true or false
access: to read data or a program in a computer, or to run a program in a computer
authorised: the one that has the computer says the person can do it
unauthorised: not authorised
knows: has it in memory as a thing that is true
reckless: makes a change, and knows that a false result can be the result of it, and makes the change all the same
touch: put a part of a person to a thing
causes: makes
cause: make
law: a list of rules for each person
guidance: words that say how to use a law
note: a part of the guidance

note 1:

```
This excludes mere physical contact with a computer and the scrutiny of data without any interaction with a computer
```

to touch a computer, or to read data out of a computer with no input to it, is not to be the one that causes the computer to run a function.

for element 1, it can not take evidence of:

```
PHYSICAL_CONTACT SCREEN_READING
```

note 2:

```
There has to be knowledge on the part of the offender that the access is unauthorised; mere recklessness is not sufficient.
```

the person has to know that the access is unauthorised. to be reckless is not to know.

for element 4, it can not take evidence of:

```
RECKLESSNESS
```

note 3:

```
an employee would only be guilty of an offence if the employer clearly defined the limits of the employee's authority
```

when the one that has the computer gives a person some access, it has to say in a list what access the person can have. access that is not in that list is unauthorised. with no list, i can not say that the access is unauthorised.

for element 3, it takes evidence of:

```
DEFINED_LIMITS
```

note 4:

```
the role of the officers in Bignell had merely been to request another to obtain information by using the computer
```

when the person says to an other person to run a computer, and the other person is authorised to run it, the person is not the one that causes the computer to run the function.

for element 1, it can not take evidence of:

```
REQUEST_TO_ANOTHER
```
